non_goals: Reading K(Z, n) as the object behind higher cohomology operations (Massey products, Toda brackets), the triangulated category as the level-1 completion, and the gap between 'every object has a finite level' and 'no finite level serves all objects' as A, are interpretations, not theorems; Massey products, triangulated categories and enhancements are not formalized here.

The historical hypothesis of the meta-level plan (Verdier's TR3, Bondal-Kapranov's enhancements, Lurie's stable infinity-categories) is not checked: the originals are not in the repository, so it stays a hypothesis.
The mathematics is standard (connectivity, truncation level and loop spaces of EM spaces); no originality is claimed. Nothing here yields ZFC |- falsum or ZFC-1 => B.

scope: Cubical Agda, --safe, nothing assumed. C-446, no finite level suffices (the all-heights version for homological algebra): for K n the Eilenberg-MacLane space K(Z, n), (1) its completion at level n+1 is contractible, equivalent to that of the point, and so at level n; (2) at level n+2 it differs from the point; a completion at level n+2 keeps K n and one at level n+1 does not (K n is not of h-level n+1), so its price is exactly n+2 and prices are unbounded; (3) K n is not contractible (down the loop space iso to Z); (4) there is no m such that contractibility after the level-m completion implies contractibility for every type, and no m such that equivalence after the level-m completion implies equivalence for every type.
